title: Joining in the round without twisting
subtitle: The single most important check before the first round of circular knitting.
excerpt: A twisted join locks a spiral into the fabric that cannot be corrected without unravelling. This tutorial explains how to check the cast-on before closing the round and how to fix a twist if you catch it in time.
sourceNotes: Circular knitting setup described in Weldon's Practical Knitter (1886), stocking-knitting series. Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), circular knitting chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: The step of verifying, before working the first round of circular knitting, that the cast-on edge faces inward consistently around the needle with no stitches twisted around the cable. A twisted join cannot be fixed after the first round without unravelling.
A small ring or clip placed on the needle to mark the beginning of each round. Slipped from the left needle to the right at the start of every round without working it.

content.text: The single most consequential step in circular knitting happens before the first stitch of the first round: checking that the cast-on edge faces consistently inward and that no stitch has crossed the cable to create a twist.

locks a spiral into the piece that cannot be corrected without unravelling back to the cast-on. This tutorial covers the check, the join, and one recovery method if you catch a twist in the first round. Difficulty: beginner (the technique is simple; the care required is everything).
Cast-on stitches on a circular needle, DPNs, or set up for magic loop

After casting on, lay the needle on a flat surface and look at the cast-on edge. Every stitch should sit with its bottom bar (the cast-on row) facing toward the centre of the needle, not twisted around the cable.

Run your left thumb along the cast-on edge to feel for any stitch that has flipped to the outside. On a circular needle, a twist at any point means the whole cast-on needs to be re-done. On DPNs, a twist on one needle can sometimes be corrected by untwisting that needle before joining.
When satisfied the cast-on is flat and untwisted, place a round marker on the right needle tip.
Hold the left needle in the left hand (with the first cast-on stitch) and the right needle (with the working yarn end) in the right hand.
Work the first stitch of the first round. The round is joined.

The join check appears at the opening of every circular-knitting pattern without exception. Hats, socks, gloves, seamless sweaters, and any project worked in the round all begin with this check. An experienced knitter does it automatically; for a new circular knitter, it is worth taking an extra 30 seconds at setup.

items.cause: A twist was present at cast-on and went unnoticed
items.fix: Unravel back to the cast-on. Re-check the edge before joining. There is no other repair.

items.symptom: Round marker falls off or gets lost
items.cause: Marker slipped off the needle tip
items.fix: Use a locking stitch marker that clips through the loop of a stitch, or use a clearly coloured marker larger than the needle tip.

items.symptom: First stitch of the round is loose
items.cause: The join stitch is naturally relaxed as the round closes
items.fix: Work the first stitch of the first round snugly. After the tail is woven in, the join closes fully.
